title: Do Self-Evolving Agents Forget? Capability Degradation and Preservation in Lifelong LLM Agent Adaptation

object.carrier: A mutable capability repository R_t updated sequentially over task distributions, instantiated four ways: an executable workflow (operator orchestration + prompt specifications, EvoAgentX on tau2-Bench), a bounded-capacity skill bank of reusable procedural reasoning templates (MemSkill-style on MATH, least-frequently-used eviction), trainable LoRA adapter parameters (STaR self-training on MedMCQA), and a persistent external memory bank of reusable strategy notes (Dynamic-Cheatsheet-style, insertion/revision/eviction)

safety_property.statement: Capability preservation under self-evolution: adapting the agent to a new task distribution must not degrade previously mastered capabilities. Capability erosion occurs when adaptation toward the current distribution increases retained risk on previously encountered distributions (L_<t(R_t) > L_<t(R_{t-1})); it manifests as retrospective capability decay, behavioral policy drift (workflows growing longer and more complex with unnecessary steps), and generalization erosion. Failure condition: unconstrained self-updates overwrite the repository structures that supported earlier behavior.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Retained old-task performance measured after evolution on new tasks, per channel: workflow - simple/complex task accuracy on tau2-Bench (Airline/Retail/Telecom) after complex-task self-evolution from a shared simple-task seed workflow, GPT-5.1 and GPT-5 nano optimizers; skill - per-domain MATH accuracy after Algebra -> Geometry -> Number Theory evolution plus retained skill usage; model - MedMCQA domain accuracy after Anatomy -> Biochemistry -> Dental sequential self-training (Qwen3-0.6B, Llama3.2-3B); memory - held-out old-task probe accuracy before vs after new-task memory updates across six domain-backbone settings (GPT-5 nano, GPT-4o mini), vanilla vs evidence-gated preservation (CPE).

capabilities: No adversary: capability erosion emerges from unconstrained self-evolution itself - each update optimized solely for the new task distribution introduces destructive interference with structures supporting earlier tasks (curvature mechanism: naive adaptation increases retained loss whenever the update direction has nonzero projection onto a positive-curvature direction of the retained-loss Hessian)
assumptions: Self-evolution is modeled as sequential adaptation over task distributions D_1, ..., D_T with a general capability state R_t that may be a workflow, skill repository, parameter state, or memory store
The local analysis assumes R_{t-1} is a local minimizer of the retained loss with Hessian H_<t positive semidefinite and sufficiently small step size eta
Vanilla and CPE variants share identical evolution pipelines, budgets, and evaluation order; only the preservation mechanism differs
not_covered: Only straightforward constraint-based instantiations of preservation are explored; adaptive regularization schedules and jointly optimized multi-component preservation frameworks are future work (Appendix I)

Experiments use controlled sequential task-distribution shifts and representative frameworks; dynamic environments, multi-agent interaction, and continuously expanding capability spaces are not covered (Appendix I)
No adaptive adversary or attack process is modeled; the measured risk is self-inflicted drift, not an external attack

intervention.name: Capability-Preserving Evolution (CPE): dimension-specific regularizers against destructive capability drift
intervention.description: A general stabilization principle constraining self-updates to acquire new capabilities while preserving capability support for prior tasks. Instantiations: (1) workflow - anchor behavioral signatures extracted from the seed workflow (core task objectives, output constraints, failure-avoidance behaviors) injected to discourage disruptive rewrites under the same optimizer and mutation budget; (2) skill/tool - capability-preserving consolidation before admission: candidates checked against preserved capability signatures, semantically related skills merged to release capacity, historically reusable high-utility skills protected from deletion; (3) model - Elastic Weight Consolidation style Fisher-based parameter-importance regularization discouraging destructive updates on parameters important to prior domains; (4) memory - evidence-gated preservation: entries accumulating repeated self-verified support are protected from destructive rewrite or eviction while low-evidence entries stay adaptable.

controls.name: Shared seed workflow / initial repository / evolution budget across variants
Pre-evolution memory state (old-domain probe accuracy before new-task updates)

results.claim: Workflow evolution: CPE improves retained simple-task performance from 41.8% to 52.8% under GPT-5.1 optimization while simultaneously achieving stronger complex-task adaptation (23.9% -> 33.4%) - mitigation does not trade against adaptation.
results.metric: tau2-Bench accuracy (%) on simple vs complex tasks after complex-task self-evolution
results.comparison: vanilla EvoAgentX vs CPE, same seed workflow and mutation budget (Table 1)
results.setting: EvoAgentX on tau2-Bench (Airline/Retail/Telecom), GPT-5.1 and GPT-5 nano optimizer backbones, parallel vanilla/CPE branches from a shared simple-task seed workflow
results.quote: For example, in workflow evolution, CPE improves retained simple-task performance from 41.8% to 52.8% under GPT-5.1 optimization while simultaneously achieving stronger complex-task adaptation.

denominator.how_counted: Accuracy averaged over the three tau2-Bench domains (Airline, Retail, Telecom) on the simple and complex task subsets after self-evolution; per-domain counts in Table 1

results.claim: Memory evolution erodes old-task retention even with frozen model parameters: across all six domain-backbone settings, average old-domain performance drops from 83.9% before new-task evolution to 81.6% after unconstrained memory updates; evidence-gated preservation (CPE) recovers retention to 83.3%.
results.metric: held-out old-domain probe accuracy (%) before vs after new-task memory evolution
results.comparison: pre-evolution memory state vs vanilla vs CPE post-evolution states (Figure 6); retention gap 2.3% -> 0.7%
results.setting: Dynamic-Cheatsheet-style external strategy repository, GPT-5 nano and GPT-4o mini solver backbones, base model fixed, six domain-backbone settings (Appendix B)
results.quote: Vanilla new-task memory evolution increases old-task interference. Across all six domain–backbone settings, average old-domain performance drops from 83.9% before new-task evolution to 81.6% after unconstrained memory updates.

denominator.how_counted: Held-out old-task probe accuracy per domain-backbone setting, averaged over the six settings; probe counts per domain not stated in the main text

results.claim: Skill evolution erodes via repository overwrite: as the distribution shifts from Geometry to Number Theory, newly synthesized skills dominate bounded repository capacity and evict previously useful Geometry skills; CPE's merge-based consolidation preserves prior-skill utilization and stabilizes retained Algebra performance.
results.metric: per-domain MATH accuracy (%) after sequential evolution + normalized retained skill usage
results.value: final-domain accuracy e.g. Number Theory 85.4 -> 87.8 (GPT-5 nano); Algebra retention stabilized under CPE
results.comparison: vanilla direct-admit + LRU eviction vs CPE merge-based consolidation (Table 2, Figure 3, Figure 4)
results.setting: MemSkill-style framework on MATH, GPT-4o mini and GPT-5 nano designer/executor backbones, sequential Algebra -> Geometry -> Number Theory evolution under identical budgets
results.quote: As the task distribution shifts from Geometry to Number Theory, newly synthesized skills gradually dominate retrieval frequency and bounded repository capacity, causing previously useful Geometry skills to become under-utilized and eventually evicted.

denominator.how_counted: Per-domain MATH evaluation accuracy after the full evolution sequence; bounded skill-bank capacity and evaluation-set sizes are in Appendix D

results.claim: Model evolution erodes via parametric overwrite (catastrophic forgetting): CPE's Fisher-based regularization preserves more retained accuracy on all evaluated domains (Qwen3-0.6B Anatomy 29.4% -> 30.5%, Biochemistry 37.2% -> 38.4%, Dental 32.2% -> 33.0%).
results.metric: MedMCQA per-domain accuracy (%) after sequential self-training
results.comparison: vanilla STaR self-training vs CPE (EWC-style regularizer), identical evolution order and LoRA configurations (Table 3)
results.setting: STaR self-training on MedMCQA, Qwen3-0.6B and Llama3.2-3B, sequential Anatomy -> Biochemistry -> Dental stages
results.quote: On Qwen3-0.6B, retained accuracy improves from 29.4% to 30.5% on Anatomy, from 37.2% to 38.4% on Biochemistry, and from 32.2% to 33.0% on Dental, with similar trends on Llama3.2-3B.

denominator.how_counted: Per-domain MedMCQA evaluation accuracy after the full three-stage evolution; evaluation-set sizes in Appendix E

results.claim: Cost reading (behavioral policy drift): unconstrained workflow evolution accumulates structural bloat - extra validation operators and detours that make the workflow over-defensive, rejecting slightly nonstandard but valid actions - and much longer workflow code; CPE substantially slows this structural growth.
results.metric: workflow complexity (code length) and post-evolution retention-adaptation trade-off
results.value: vanilla accumulates much longer workflow code; CPE slows expansion (Figure 2b)
results.comparison: vanilla vs CPE from the same seed workflow (Figure 2a-c)
results.setting: EvoAgentX complex-task self-evolution, per-domain workflow code length tracked during evolution (Figure 2)
results.quote: This structural drift is reflected in Figure 2(b), where vanilla EvoAgentX accumulates much longer workflow code, while CPE substantially slows this expansion.

denominator.how_counted: Workflow code length measured during self-evolution on the complex Airline task subset; post-evolution workflows evaluated on simple and complex subsets

results.claim: Memory-channel summary: CPE's evidence-gated preservation reduces the average old-task retention gap caused by new-task memory updates from 2.3% to 0.7%.
results.metric: average retention gap (percentage points) across six domain-backbone settings
results.setting: Same memory-evolution setup as Appendix B, summarized in §4.4
results.quote: CPE mitigates this interference through evidence-gated preservation, protecting historically reliable memories while keeping low-evidence entries adaptable, reducing the average retention gap from 2.3% to 0.7%.

denominator.how_counted: Gap between pre-evolution and post-evolution old-domain probe accuracy, averaged over the six domain-backbone settings

limitations.statement: Only lightweight, domain-specific preservation instantiations are explored; adaptive schedules and jointly optimized multi-component frameworks are left open.
limitations.quote: Accordingly, the preservation mechanisms used in this paper are intentionally lightweight and domain-specific, including anchor-based workflow regularization, repository consolidation, Fisher-style parameter constraints, and memory preservation heuristics. More sophisticated preservation strategies, adaptive regularization schedules, or jointly optimized multi-component preservation frameworks may further improve the stability–plasticity tradeoff in long-horizon self-evolving agents.

limitations.statement: Experiments cover controlled sequential distribution shifts on representative frameworks; real-world open-ended evolution trajectories (dynamic environments, multi-agent interaction, expanding capability spaces) are future work.
limitations.quote: In addition, our experiments focus on controlled sequential task-distribution shifts and representative self-evolution frameworks. Real-world autonomous agents may encounter substantially more complex and open-ended evolution trajectories, including dynamic environments, multi-agent interaction, and continuously expanding capability spaces. Extending CPE to such settings remains an important direction for future work.

reproduction.data: tau2-Bench (Airline/Retail/Telecom simple+complex subsets), MATH (Algebra/Geometry/Number Theory), MedMCQA (Anatomy/Biochemistry/Dental), Dynamic-Cheatsheet-style memory repository; backbones GPT-5.1, GPT-5 nano, GPT-4o mini, Qwen3-0.6B, Llama3.2-3B; frameworks EvoAgentX, MemSkill-style, STaR
